newsitem.title: UK: Options-Coffee vols soar further, cocoa sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Options-Coffee vols soar further, cocoa sidelined.

text.p: Coffee options trading turned quiet this week after Wednesday's March expiry but volatilities remained at steep levels amid continued sharp swings on the futures market.
Cocoa options were completely sidelined with no interest being expressed from either side of the market. The interest was further dampened by prolonged stability on the underlying futures front.
In coffee, traders noted selling of May $2,000 calls against $1,650 puts on Thursday.

The May $2,000 calls were traded at a hefty 55 percent volatility and May $1,650 puts at 42 percent. The May $1,650, $1,550 and $1,450 puts saw volatilities at 43-45 percent last week, which were up from 37-38 percent a week earlier.
"These levels seem to be high and they are holding relatively steady," said one options trader. Ten-day volatility is seen at 44 percent.
Activity was mainly dominated by volatility traders.
Robusta futures, shadowing the often volatile New York-traded arabicas, retraced sharply from last week's peak of $1,718 a tonne basis May, a six-month high, to a low of $1,460 this week.
But prices have since climbed back to trade around $1,540 level late Friday afternoon.
London has accumulated some 45 percent since early January and traders said this week's pullback could be seen as a technical downward correction.
Sentiment was also further dampened by news of the end of a strike in Colombia.
But traders won't rule out a further rally.
The size of the coming 1997/98 Brazilian crop holds the key to future direction. This week's Brazilian industry forecasts put the yield at 23 million bags or below.

But traders said even at 25 million, it would be insufficient to meet world demand and with roasters maintaining their hand-to-mouth buying programme, any supply disruption from weather or other causes will keep the market unnerved for the rest of the year.
As expected, March options went into expiry on Wednesday without any fireworks.
"There was no trading on the morning of the expiry," said one trader.
Cocoa was barely traded this week, except some May 850 and 950 calls on Monday and Tuesday.
"There was some origin buying of calls but the market is not interested," said one market maker.
The futures market continued to languish in a narrow $871-$885 band this week as the market adjusted to sterling's fluctuations against the major units.
There were little technical or fundamental inputs to lure the market out of the current range.
The main influencing factor will be the Ivorian arrivals, which have so far shown no signs of tailing off with the total main crop almost approaching last year's record level.
There have been a dry and hot spell in Ivory Coast but some said it would not cause major damage to mid-crop yields.
-- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
